Task Name: F01 – Staff accounts and secure sign-in
Description:
Value: Every action in the system is done by a known person.

Scope:
- Individual staff accounts (name, email, role, department)
- Sign in / sign out, forgotten password, session timeout
- Add, edit and deactivate staff (no deletion of history)
- Audit trail of sign-ins and account changes

Not in this feature: Charity (partner) accounts → F03; custom roles → F29

Depends on: None
BRD use cases: UC01, UC08, UC09
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an active staff account, when the user signs in with correct credentials, then their home page opens
2. Given wrong credentials, when the user signs in, then access is refused with a generic message
3. Given a deactivated account, when the user tries to sign in, then access is refused
4. Given any sign-in or account change, then it is recorded with user and time

Description:
Value: Each person sees only the menus, pages and actions of their role.

Scope:
- Fixed system roles: Admin, Grants Manager, Reviewer, Committee Secretary, Project Manager, Finance, CEO
- Menu and home page per role
- Access enforced by the system on every page and action, not only by hiding menus
- Departments list for organizing staff

Not in this feature: Editable / custom roles → F29

Depends on: F01
BRD use cases: UC02, UC11
Decision needed: Q149 — should system roles be editable? (does not block: fixed roles ship first)
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a Reviewer, when they open the system, then only their sections appear in the menu
2. Given a user opens a page outside their role by link, then the system blocks it with an access-denied message
3. Given the Admin changes a user's role, then the new access applies at the next action

Description:
Value: Charities register online instead of sending papers.

Scope:
- Registration with licence number, organization data and delegate details
- Delegate mobile / email verification by one-time code
- Required documents upload (licence, delegate authorization)
- Registration status visible to the applicant

Not in this feature: Joining an already registered charity → F05

Depends on: F02
BRD use cases: UC39
Decision needed: Which identity verification is required for delegates (OTP only, or national ID)?
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a new licence number, when the delegate completes the form and verifies the code, then a registration request is created with status Pending
2. Given a licence number already registered, then the system stops a duplicate registration
3. Given a missing required document, then the request cannot be submitted

Task Name: F04 – Registration review and partner register
Description:
Value: One trusted register of approved charities.

Scope:
- Queue of registration requests with documents
- Approve / return / reject with reason
- On approval: charity record and delegate account created
- Partner directory with search, filters and Excel export
- Add a charity manually and invite its delegate to activate the account

Not in this feature: Bank verification and licence updates → F06

Depends on: F03
BRD use cases: UC49, UC50, UC56, UC57
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a pending request, when the Grants Manager approves it, then the charity appears in the register and the delegate can sign in
2. Given a request is returned or rejected, then a reason is mandatory and the applicant sees it
3. Given the directory, when the user filters by status, then only matching charities are listed

Task Name: F05 – Charity portal access and team
Description:
Value: Charities manage their own users without calling the foundation.

Scope:
- Charity users sign in to the portal; choose the charity if they belong to more than one
- Primary delegate adds / deactivates team members (project manager, finance, member)
- Transfer of the primary delegation
- Join request to an existing charity

Depends on: F04
BRD use cases: UC40, UC41, UC55
Decision needed: Can one person belong to more than one charity? (open comment in BRD)
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a primary delegate, when they add a team member, then that person can sign in to the charity portal
2. Given a non-delegate member, then they cannot add or remove team members
3. Given the delegation is transferred, then the old delegate loses delegate rights immediately

Description:
Value: Funding goes only to verified charities and verified bank accounts.

Scope:
- Charity 360 profile: data, documents, decision history
- Confirm or block a charity (with reason)
- Bank account (IBAN certificate) verification by staff
- Licence / official data update requested by the charity and reviewed by staff

Depends on: F05
BRD use cases: UC46, UC51, UC52, UC53, UC54
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a charity uploads a new IBAN certificate, then the account stays Unverified until staff verify it
2. Given a blocked charity, then it cannot submit new applications
3. Given any confirm / block / verify decision, then it appears in the charity's history with user and time

Task Name: F07 – Annual plan and budget structure
Description:
Value: The annual budget is defined in the system instead of spreadsheets.

Scope:
- Create the annual plan with total budget
- Plan tree: tracks → items → initiatives with budget per level
- Edits recorded with an evidence document
- Warning when child budgets exceed the parent

Not in this feature: Budget adjustments and plan lock → F24; endowments → F25

Depends on: F02
BRD use cases: UC19, UC20, UC21
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a new plan, when levels are added, then the tree shows each level's budget and the plan total
2. Given children budgets exceed the parent, then the system warns before saving
3. Given changes are saved, then an evidence document is required and the change is in the plan history

Description:
Value: The foundation announces calls for grants in one place.

Scope:
- Create opportunity: name, description, budget, plan item, open / close dates
- Application form from a simple form builder (fields, required flags)
- Draft → Published → Closed status
- Opportunity list with status and application count

Not in this feature: Eligibility targeting and invitations → F10; workflow templates → F28

Depends on: F07
BRD use cases: UC13, UC28, UC29, UC30, UC31
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a draft opportunity, then it is not visible to charities until published
2. Given a published opportunity, when the close date passes, then it stops accepting applications
3. Given the opportunity budget exceeds the plan item's available budget, then the system refuses to save

Task Name: F09 – Opportunities on the public page and portal
Description:
Value: Charities find open grants without contacting the foundation.

Scope:
- Public landing page listing published, open opportunities
- Portal list of opportunities the charity can apply to
- Opportunity details page with dates, budget and conditions

Not in this feature: Filtering by eligibility → F10

Depends on: F08
BRD use cases: UC03, UC42
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a published opportunity within its dates, then it appears on the public page and in the portal
2. Given a visitor who is not signed in clicks Apply, then they are asked to sign in or register

Task Name: F10 – Eligibility, partner groups and invitations
Description:
Value: Only the right charities can apply to each opportunity.

Scope:
- Eligibility rules per opportunity (applicant type, region, groups)
- Partner groups for targeting
- Private invitations to selected charities
- Limit of applications per charity

Depends on: F09
BRD use cases: UC32, UC36, UC43, UC58
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a charity that does not meet the rules, then the opportunity is not offered to it and it cannot apply
2. Given an invited charity, when it opens the invitation, then it can apply even if the opportunity is private
3. Given the per-charity limit is reached, then a new application is refused

Description:
Value: Applications arrive complete and in one place.

Scope:
- Fill the opportunity's form in the portal, save as draft
- Required attachments per opportunity
- Requested amount, duration and bill of quantities (items)
- Submit with confirmation; application number generated

Not in this feature: AI pre-fill → F30

Depends on: F09
BRD use cases: UC44
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a missing required field or attachment, then the application cannot be submitted
2. Given a submitted application, then the charity sees it with status Submitted and cannot edit it
3. Given the opportunity is closed, then submission is refused

Description:
Value: Every staff member sees their pending work in one list.

Scope:
- Inbox with tasks assigned to me, due dates and overdue flags
- Manual tasks: create, assign, change status, comment
- Meetings with date and attendees
- List and calendar views

Not in this feature: Bulk decisions and focus mode → F27

Depends on: F02
BRD use cases: UC90, UC91, UC92, UC93
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a task is assigned to a user, then it appears in their inbox with its due date
2. Given a task passes its due date, then it is flagged overdue
3. Given a manual task, then only its creator or assignee can change it

Description:
Value: Applications move through Reception → Study → Approval with clear owners and SLAs.

Scope:
- Review queue per stage with filters
- Application dossier: data, attachments, history
- Stage decision: approve to next stage, return for edits, reject (reason required)
- Stage tasks created automatically in My Tasks with SLA days

Not in this feature: Scoring and pass score → F14; committee minutes → F16; AI evaluation → F30

Depends on: F11, F12
BRD use cases: UC59, UC60, UC62, UC88
Decision needed: Are the three stages fixed, or configurable per opportunity?
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an application at a stage, then a task is created for that stage's owners
2. Given a reviewer approves, then the application moves to the next stage and the history records who and when
3. Given a rejection, then a reason is mandatory and the charity is notified

Task Name: F14 – Evaluation criteria and pass score
Description:
Value: Applications are scored consistently and weak ones cannot be approved by mistake.

Scope:
- Evaluation criteria with weights per opportunity
- Reviewers score each criterion with notes
- Pass score: approval blocked below it, wherever the decision is taken

Depends on: F13
BRD use cases: UC33
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given criteria weights that do not total 100%, then they cannot be saved
2. Given the total score is below the pass score, then approval is blocked
3. Given a scored application, then the dossier shows each reviewer's score and notes

Task Name: F15 – Charity follow-up and requested edits
Description:
Value: Charities see where their application is and respond quickly.

Scope:
- Application status and expected reply date in the portal
- Returned for edits: charity edits the data / attachments and resubmits
- Staff-proposed changes to amounts or quantities accepted or refused by the charity

Depends on: F13
BRD use cases: UC45, UC63
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an application is returned for edits, then the charity can change its data and resubmit to the same stage
2. Given staff propose a new amount, then it applies only after the charity accepts it
3. Given a final decision, then the charity sees the decision and reason

Description:
Value: Committee decisions are recorded once and applied to all the applications they cover.

Scope:
- Committee secretary selects applications at the Approval stage
- Minute with date, members, decision per application and the signed minute file
- Decisions applied to all selected applications in one step

Depends on: F14
BRD use cases: UC64, UC95
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a minute is saved with decisions, then each application moves according to its decision
2. Given a minute without the signed file, then it cannot be finalized
3. Given an application decided by minute, then its history links to the minute

Task Name: F17 – Contract and project from an approved application
Description:
Value: Approved grants become signed contracts and trackable projects without retyping.

Scope:
- Contract generated from the application (parties, amount, items, payment schedule)
- Payment schedule as % of amount per milestone
- Contract signing status
- Project created with budget and project manager

Not in this feature: Splitting one application into several projects → F33

Depends on: F16
BRD use cases: UC67, UC69, UC70, UC71
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an approved application, when the Grants Manager transfers it, then one contract and one project are created with the approved amount
2. Given the payment schedule does not total 100%, then the transfer is refused
3. Given a contract is not signed, then project execution cannot start

Task Name: F18 – Project plan and start of execution
Description:
Value: Each project has an agreed plan before work starts.

Scope:
- Project plan: milestones, activities, due dates, linked payments
- Start execution (requires signed contract and complete plan)
- Project portfolio list with status and overdue (stalled) flag

Not in this feature: Plan changes after start → F20

Depends on: F17
BRD use cases: UC72, UC74
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a signed contract and a complete plan, when the project manager starts execution, then the project status becomes In progress
2. Given an activity passes its due date without approval, then the project is flagged stalled

Task Name: F19 – Charity progress reports and milestone approval
Description:
Value: Progress is proven with evidence before money is released.

Scope:
- Charity submits task progress, evidence files and milestone reports in the portal
- Project manager verifies evidence: accept or return with note
- Milestone approved → its payment becomes due

Not in this feature: Indicators → F33

Depends on: F18
BRD use cases: UC47, UC75, UC76
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a charity submits a milestone report with evidence, then the project manager gets a task to verify it
2. Given evidence is returned, then the charity sees the note and can resubmit
3. Given a milestone is approved, then its linked payment becomes Due

Task Name: F20 – Plan revisions and project closure
Description:
Value: Changes and closure are controlled and documented.

Scope:
- Request a plan revision with reason; approved by a different person
- Close the project after all milestones are approved, with a final evaluation

Depends on: F19
BRD use cases: UC77, UC78
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a revision request, then the requester cannot approve it
2. Given unapproved milestones, then the project cannot be closed
3. Given a project is closed, then no new tasks or payments can be added

Description:
Value: No payment is released without the required approvals.

Scope:
- Due payments list per project
- Submit a due payment for approval
- Three-level approval: project manager → Grants Manager → CEO; reject with reason returns it to Due
- Approval tasks created in My Tasks

Depends on: F19
BRD use cases: UC80, UC81, UC89
Decision needed: Are there amount thresholds that change the approval chain?
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a due payment is submitted, then the project's manager gets an approval task
2. Given step 1 is approved, then the Grants Manager gets the next task; after step 2 the CEO
3. Given any rejection, then a reason is mandatory and the payment returns to Due
4. Given a person approved one step, then they cannot approve another step of the same payment

Task Name: F22 – Disbursement order, transfer and receipt
Description:
Value: Finance pays the right account and every payment is closed with proof.

Scope:
- Disbursement order issued after final approval
- Payee confirmed (charity's verified bank account; third party only with re-approval)
- Finance records the bank transfer and uploads the transfer notice
- Charity uploads the receipt voucher; payment closed as Paid

Depends on: F21, F06
BRD use cases: UC82, UC83, UC84
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a payment is fully approved, then a disbursement order is issued with a unique number
2. Given the bank account is not verified, then the transfer cannot be recorded
3. Given the payee is changed after approval, then the approval chain restarts
4. Given the receipt voucher is uploaded, then the payment status becomes Paid

Description:
Value: Finance and management see every payment and what is still owed.

Scope:
- Payments register with status, partner, project and amounts
- Commitments per charity (scheduled vs paid)
- Excel export

Depends on: F22
BRD use cases: UC79, UC85
Decision needed: Single definition of “paid” (after transfer or after receipt?)
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the register, then each payment shows its current status and who it waits for
2. Given a charity, then its committed, due and paid totals add up to its contracts' amounts

Description:
Value: The foundation always knows used, committed, paid and available budget.

Scope:
- Live budget figures per plan level: committed, due, paid, available
- Budget increase / decrease / transfer with evidence document
- Financial operations register and plan history
- Lock and reopen the plan

Depends on: F23
BRD use cases: UC22, UC23, UC24, UC25
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a contract is signed, then the plan item's committed amount increases by the contract amount
2. Given a decrease larger than the available amount, then it is refused
3. Given any adjustment, then an evidence document is required and the operation is in the register

Description:
Value: Each endowment's share of the plan and its use are visible.

Scope:
- Register endowments (funding sources)
- Record endowment funding
- Endowment share per plan level and endowment report

Depends on: F24
BRD use cases: UC16, UC26, UC27
Decision needed: How are endowment shares decided (equal, by size, manual)?
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given endowments participate in a plan item, then the item's budget is split by their shares
2. Given an endowment is used in a plan, then it cannot be deleted

Description:
Value: Management gets the numbers without asking the team.

Scope:
- Dashboard: budget, applications by stage, projects, payments, delays
- Standard reports (applications, projects, payments, partners) with filters and Excel export
- Staff workload and performance view

Depends on: F23
BRD use cases: UC12, UC86, UC87
Decision needed: Which reports does management request today?
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given the dashboard, then figures match the registers they come from
2. Given a report with filters, when exported, then the Excel file contains the same rows

Description:
Value: Staff spend less time navigating and deciding.

Scope:
- Global search across partners, applications, projects and payments
- Saved views and list exports
- Decide directly from a task, and bulk decisions
- Focus mode for processing tasks one by one

Depends on: F13, F21
BRD use cases: UC04, UC06, UC07, UC94, UC96
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a search term, then results show only records the user may access
2. Given a decision from a task or focus mode, then the same rules apply as on the application page (e.g. pass score)

Description:
Value: Admins reuse setups and every sensitive change is traceable.

Scope:
- Workflow templates reusable across opportunities
- Communication templates and reference lists
- Applicant types open / closed for registration
- Sensitive configuration changes require an evidence document and keep history

Depends on: F13
BRD use cases: UC14, UC15, UC18, UC34, UC38
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a template is applied to an opportunity, then its stages and criteria are copied
2. Given a sensitive setting is changed, then an evidence document is required and the old value is kept in history

Description:
Value: The foundation adapts access to its own structure.

Scope:
- Permission matrix (view / write / delete) by role
- Create custom roles, optionally copying a system role
- Enable / disable permissions for a whole role, with change history

Depends on: F02
BRD use cases: UC10
Decision needed: Q149 — may system roles be edited, or only custom roles?
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a permission is disabled for a role, then every user with that role loses it at their next action
2. Given a custom role is assigned to staff, then it cannot be deleted
3. Given any permission change, then it is recorded with user, time and before / after

Description:
Value: AI saves time on forms and evaluation while people keep every decision.

Scope:
- AI pre-fill of application forms from uploaded documents (charity confirms)
- AI document check on attachments (advisory)
- AI evaluation summary for reviewers and external AI evaluation report
- AI assistant for questions on grant data (read-only, proposes links)

Depends on: F13
BRD use cases: UC05, UC48, UC61
Decision needed: Which AI provider, and what data may be sent to it?
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given AI proposes values, then nothing is saved until the user confirms
2. Given an AI check flags a document, then the user can still proceed (advisory only)
3. Given the AI assistant answers, then it uses only data the user may access

Description:
Value: The foundation can grant products from its stock, not only money.

Scope:
- Product catalog with stock
- Product opportunities and product requests
- Approval deducts stock; delivery recorded

Depends on: F14
BRD use cases: UC35, UC68
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given a request above available stock, then it is refused
2. Given a product grant is approved, then stock is deducted once and delivery is tracked

Description:
Value: The foundation can tender a defined project and award the best offer.

Scope:
- Define the tendered project (scope, deliverables, budget)
- Invited charities submit offers; side-by-side comparison
- Award to one evaluated offer; others closed with notice; contract and project created

Depends on: F17
BRD use cases: UC37
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an offer above the budget, then it is refused
2. Given an RFP is awarded, then only an evaluated offer above the pass score can win
3. Given an award, then all other offers are closed and notified

Task Name: F33 – Multi-project grants, merges and funding conditions
Description:
Value: Complex grants are handled without workarounds.

Scope:
- Split one application into several projects
- Merge applications of the same charity
- Funding conditions, co-funding and indicators
- Internal initiatives run by the foundation

Depends on: F17
BRD use cases: UC65, UC66, UC73
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given an application is split, then the projects' budgets total the approved amount
2. Given co-funding conditions are unconfirmed, then final approval is blocked
3. Given merged applications, then one contract is created

Description:
Value: Several grantor foundations can use the same platform separately.

Scope:
- Platform admin registers and suspends grantor organizations
- Strict data isolation between organizations

Depends on: F02
BRD use cases: UC17
Decision needed: Is Manih for one foundation or several?
Acceptance Criteria:
1. Given two organizations, then users of one never see the other's data
2. Given an organization is suspended, then its users cannot sign in
